outline.rationale: The user is a total beginner whose explicit goal is conceptual understanding ("how it works"), not building or deploying. So I excluded all tooling, coding, libraries, and project-setup nodes, and avoided math-heavy derivations. The outline is intuition-first and conceptual. Node 1 establishes the fundamental paradigm shift (data vs. explicit rules). Node 2 explains the core mechanism of learning at a high level. Node 3 maps the landscape of approaches (MECE categories). Node 4 demystifies training without formulas, building on the learning concept. Node 5 addresses failure modes, which is essential for genuine understanding of why ML works the way it does. Node 6 covers neural networks specifically since a beginner will inevitably encounter the term and want intuition. Node 7 covers evaluation — understanding how trust is established. Node 8 grounds everything in relatable real-world examples, which serves a conceptual learner well. Ordering reflects dependency: concept → mechanism → types → training → limits → a key architecture → evaluation → application, though several middle nodes are loosely parallel.
